newsitem.title: USA: Caterpillar 12 pct Q2 EPS gain seen.
newsitem.headline: Caterpillar 12 pct Q2 EPS gain seen.

text.p: Heavy equipment manufacturer Caterpillar Inc is expected to post about a 12 percent earnings per share gain for the second quarter, boosted by strong shipments to the U.S. construction market.

"Their shipments continue to outpace the overall business of the industry," said Lisa Shalett, analyst with Sanford C. Bernstein. She noted that Caterpillar intentionally cut inventories previously to become more attuned to industry demand.
The mean analyst estimate for the company's second quarter is $1.09 a share, according to First Call. That's up from $0.97 a share a year ago, adjusting for a recent two-for-one stock split.
Caterpillar, which well exceeded Wall Street estimates in the first quarter, is scheduled to release earnings Tuesday morning. The company declined to comment on earnings estimates.

"I think they're going to have another good quarter," said J. Blair Brumley, analyst at Dain Bosworth Inc. "There's nothing in the realm of the sales that they've been talking about that would lead you to believe otherwise."

Caterpillar expressed concern about the dollar's strength against the yen and the prospect for greater-than-expected Federal Reserve tightening when it reported first quarter earnings in April. But since then the dollar has retreated against the yen and the Fed has not tightened.

While the dollar strengthened in recent weeks against the Deutschemark, analysts said they expected the European market to be soft for Caterpillar, so the currency factor there should have less impact.
Analysts are mixed on their expectations in Europe in 1998 for Cateprillar and the company is not expected to give a forecast in the second quarter earnings statement.

"The thing that we're most intrigued about going forward is what Europe is going to look like in 1998," Brumley said. "We suspect that Europe is going to be a very, very good market for them next year."
But Shalett said that budget constraints by European countries trying to meet criteria for joining the European Monetary Union could hamper demand for construction equipment in 1998.
"Our view continues to be that there are real structural impediments in Europe," Shalett said.
Caterpillar shares were up 2-1/4 at 56-5/8 Monday.
